findings.reason: without a declared dependency on sn-house-style §2 the Distinct arm has no reachable template to edit, and the same missing-dependency defect was already corrected once for §3.
findings.text: §4's "Distinct" ruling is "The house-style template for each gains the sentence that separates them", but that template is `templates.yml` delivered by sn-house-style §2 (keyed by the pattern family §2 of this plan produces), and §4 declares only `sn-integrity-backlog#s6`, so a node built from §4 either edits an artifact another plan owns or stalls on one that has not landed

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `domain_priority.py`, `workers.py`, `consolidation.py`, `audits.py`, `context.py`, `vocab_semantic_dedup.py`, `dd_domain_classifier.py`, census §4–§7, sn-judgment-evaluation §5/§7 and sn-integrity-backlog §6 all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §3's done-when now carries a negative control ("it fails with the lookup removed"), and §4's control declination stands unchanged since it delivers recorded rulings rather than a guard.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no gate or worklist is routed to a scratchpad or node-local temporary path; §3 records a before/after census and §4 a recorded ruling per overlap.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a code symbol; the only version-like strings are the live model seat `gpt-5.5` and plan-section references in prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §3's root cause matches census §5 (domains follow the source), its mechanism reaches the confirmed single approval point, and the caller (`consolidate_candidates`' approved-list loop) is named.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 delivers domain assignment by quantity and §4 delivers near-duplicate adjudication, each on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §4 rules "Distinct" overlaps by editing "the house-style template", which is `templates.yml` delivered by sn-house-style §2, but §4 declares only `sn-integrity-backlog#s6`.
